children: Basis bids for soybeans and corn loaded on barges and delivered to U.S. Gulf Coast terminals continued to ease on Tuesday, as a rally in crop futures prices fueled a flurry of farmer sales in the cash markets, traders said.
The U.S. Department of Agriculture on Tuesday confirmed exporters sold 136,000 metric tons of U.S. soybeans to China for delivery in the 2026/27 marketing year.
CIF soybean barges loaded in split-September traded at 106 cents over Chicago Board of Trade November (SX26) futures. Loadings in October traded at 109 cents over CBOT November futures.
Meanwhile, CIF soybean basis bids for barges loaded in August were down 4 cents at about 99 cents over CBOT November futures, and September barges were bid at 101 cents over November futures.
FOB basis offers were steady at about 125 cents over futures for soybeans loaded in early September and late September.
For corn, CIF basis bids for barges loaded in September were bid at 66 cents over CBOT December (CZ26) corn futures, while October loadings were bid at 86 cents over December corn futures.
And barges loaded in October-November-December traded at 92 cents over December corn futures.
FOB corn export premiums for shipments in September were steady, with offers at around 111 cents over futures for shipments in late September.
